chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, who said:
I saw Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام in the litter; he performed sajdah upon paper, and most of that time he would indicate by gesturing.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first report, because the purport of the first report is a type of karāhah, and he explicitly stated that in his saying that he disliked making sajdah upon paper that has writing on it. Thus the two reports are to be understood as indicating permissibility. Also, the report of Ṣafwān al-Jammāl, in which he narrated the action of Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, does not state that the paper upon which he was making sajdah had writing on it; rather, the karāhah is directed only to that which has this description. It is possible that it had no writing, and thus it accords with the first report.

key_terms.الْقِرْطَاسِ: paper or writing sheet used as the surface for sajdah
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikedness; a ruling of reprehensibility rather than prohibition
key_terms.الْمَحْمِلِ: a riding litter or carriage in which one travels
key_terms.يُومِئُ: he indicates by gesture rather than full bodily movement

ai.seo_question: Is sajdah on paper permissible, especially when the paper has writing on it?
ai.summary: This report describes Imām Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام making sajdah on paper while in a litter, and then explains how this can be reconciled with another report that expresses dislike for such a practice. The resolution given is that sajdah on paper is permissible in principle, while karāhah applies specifically when the paper contains writing.
